name: Oak Tree
intro: An oak is a big, strong tree. Its seeds are called acorns.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: An oak is a big tree with a wide top.
A grown oak can be as tall as a 10-story building.
Many oak leaves have round bumps called lobes.
In spring, it has long yellow flowers called catkins.
Its acorns sit in little cups.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Oak trees grow in the top half of the world.
Some grow where it is cool.
Some grow where it is warm.
North America has many kinds of oaks.
In England, oaks grow in many woods.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: An oak needs sunlight, water, and good soil.
Young oaks grow best in full sun.
They like soil where water drains away.
Young trees need water each week if it does not rain.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: An oak tree starts as an acorn.
Ripe acorns turn brown and fall to the ground.
A root grows out of the acorn first.
A tiny tree sprouts in the spring.
An oak makes its first acorns when it is about 20 years old.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Squirrels and jays bury acorns to eat later.
Some forgotten acorns grow into new oak trees.
Birds, bugs, and bats live in oak trees.
One big oak can make thousands of acorns in a year.
Some oak trees live for hundreds of years.

vocab.meaning: The nut of an oak tree that has a seed inside.
Long, hanging flowers on some trees.
Round bumps on the edge of a leaf.
To start to grow out of a seed.
